examples.knowledge_point: Finding Solutions of Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm: Advanced Cases
examples.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, determine the value of $x$ that satisfies the equation $5^{x+2}=9^{x-2}.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $\left(\ln\right)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{x+2} & ={9}^{x-2} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({5}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({9}^{x-2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify both sides of the equation. This gives

$$
(x+2)\ln(5) = (x-2)\ln(9).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =(x-2)\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9) & =-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)+2\operatorname{ln}⁡(5) \\ x(\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)) & =2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)) \\ x & =\frac{2(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡(9))}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(9)-\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x-2} & ={10}^{-3x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x-2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{-3x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x-2=\operatorname{ln}⁡({10}^{-3x}).
$$

Next, we use the power law of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
x-2=-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x-2 & =-3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) \\ x+3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(10) & =2 \\ x(1+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)) & =2 \\ x & =\frac{2}{1+3\operatorname{ln}⁡(10)}\end{aligned}
$$
